prompt: A rectangle has corners $(-3, 1)$, $(4, 1)$, $(4, 5)$, $(-3, 5)$. Find its **area**.
hint: The area of a rectangle is its width times its height. Both lengths can be read from the coordinates of the corners.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Count across in two parts: from $x = -3$ to the y-axis, then from the y-axis to $x = 4$. That total is the width.
The area of a rectangle is its width times its height. Both lengths can be read from the coordinates of the corners.
The width is the gap between the $x$-values: $|4 - (-3)| = 7$. The height is the gap between the $y$-values: $|5 - 1| = 4$. Multiply them.
$7 \times 4 = 28$, so the area is $28$ square units.

explanation: The bottom side runs from $(-3, 1)$ to $(4, 1)$, so the width is $|4 - (-3)| = 4 + 3 = 7$.
The right side runs from $(4, 1)$ to $(4, 5)$, so the height is $|5 - 1| = 4$.
The area of a rectangle is width times height: $7 \times 4$.
$7 \times 4 = 28$, so the area is $28$ square units.
